judged_text: updateEvent's fallback branch evaluates event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) inside the branch where externalCalendarId is already falsy, so the search compares externalIds against a null/undefined key, always returns undefined, and calendar.events.update is invoked with calendarId: undefined. Rescheduling any booking whose stored reference lacks externalCalendarId (every booking created through the no-credentialId destination branch, which passes no externalId to CalendarManager.createEvent) fails the Google update with a missing/invalid-calendarId error that CalendarManager swallows as a failure result, leaving the Google event at the old time while the Cal.com booking and attendee emails show the new time.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new fallback logic in `updateEvent` sets `selectedCalendar` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` specifically in the branch where `externalCalendarId` is falsy. That means it is searching for a calendar whose `externalId` equals `undefined`/`null`, which will almost always return `undefined`, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined`. Unlike `createEvent` (which explicitly falls back to `"primary"` with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`), the diff does not show any similar fallback for `updateEvent`, making it very plausible that Google update calls will be issued with an invalid/undefined `calendarId` (or at minimum the calendar selection will be wrong). This defect is directly introduced by the changed `.find(...)` predicate using `externalCalendarId` as the lookup key in the falsy branch.
